chapter: New York, Nick's and the Army
title: The Army-authorized Dixieland band at Asheville and Fud Livingston's arrangements
summary: Because men kept being reassigned he got the Army to pay for arrangements, many by Fud Livingston, and his band played officers' clubs.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, I guess it was the only one I know of and the reason for it was that I needed--- they were changing men on me all the time; there was a point of redistribution and I would be losing guys; they'd be sending

them out to other assignments and, so, I had to have music; if I lost a guy and if I had a guy who could read, our band could go on--- so, the Army paid for those arrangements and Fud Livingston made a lot of arrangements for me while I was in the Army.
Well, he was in Florida at that time but---
He wasn't in the Army - well, he was too old - way too old---

No but then too he had a whole series of arrangements for small bands that sold in music stores. I got all those and some he made for me as well, but he got paid by the United States Army. It was--- musically, a success for me in the Army; I was with the Marching Band -- the Concert Band -- the Cocktail Orchestras, playing by the soldiers ate their noon meals and such things; I did all of that.
But, my band - of course, was the most popular because it was a Dixieland band and we played all the Officers' Clubs--
